svg.aria-label: L1 data cache: 128 KiB, 8 ways, 64 B lines, virtually indexed
svg.text: L1 data cache: 128 KiB, 8 ways, 64 B lines, virtually indexed
The classic address split, tag and data arrays, comparators and mux, with the bits the M1 uses and the micro tag that picks the way before the TLB answers.
16 KiB pages: bits 13:0 are the page offset, no translation needed
Helper bits, per line and per set
Tree PLRU over 8 ways: the victim is found by following the 7 bits
One load hit, cycle by cycle
VA 47:14, page number: to the dTLB, and folded to the utag
one 64 B line is 4 banks (bits 7:6 pick
which); a 16 B load touches 1 bank, an LDP
Q touches 2; three loads a cycle when their
banks differ or piggyback on one element
early: fold(VA 47:14) against the eight utags of the
set picks one way in cycle 1. Measured as
AMD-style; an alias reads the wrong way and
late: the dTLB page number against the chosen
way's tag in cycle 3. A mismatch replays the load;
3 cycles to a pointer chase, 4 to an ALU
A store miss takes a store-miss entry and
fetches the line for ownership while
younger stores that hit write ahead.
Each bit points away from the most recent access; a hit flips the bits
on its path. Here the victim is way 7. Prime+Retouch reproduced the
PACMAN saw only 4 effective ways in an eviction test. Proposed:
utag aliasing hides half the ways from a VA-only probe, so it
cycle 1: the fold of VA 47:14 picks way 3 from the utags
cycle 2: the set and bank read 16 B from that way, data goes out
cycle 3: the PA tag of way 3 confirms the hit, or the load replays
